info.title: epiloYES internal HTTP API
info.summary: Public reader endpoints, editorial writes behind a bearer JWT, and the operational probes served by the Go binary.
info.description:
Machine-readable description of what the Go binary actually serves. It is written from the handlers, not from prose: where this document and `specs/001-epiloyes-alpha/contracts/http-api.md` disagree, the handlers won and this document follows them.

**Topology.** The API is not publicly routable. In every deployment (compose, Cloudflare, Kubernetes) it listens on an internal network and the Astro server is the only public HTTP surface. As defence in depth every response - this document included - carries `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.

**Errors.** Every handler-produced error is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` body: `type` (always `about:blank`), `title` (the plain rendering of the status code), `status`, and `detail` (omitted when empty). See the `Problem` schema.

**Pagination.** Lists take `limit` (default 20) and `cursor` (opaque, keyset) and answer `{ items, next_cursor }`, where `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page. A `limit` outside 1-100 is rejected with 400 rather than clamped; a malformed or oversized `cursor` is rejected with 400.

**Auth.** Only the editorial endpoints require authentication: `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`, verified against the configured JWKS, and the subject's account must hold the editor role. The database enforces the same rule again on write. When `JWKS_URL` is unset the whole `/api/v1/editorial/` prefix is left unmounted deliberately, and those paths answer 404 instead of authenticating nobody.

**Unrouted paths under `/api/v1/`.** Each half of the namespace owns a catch-all. The content module answers everything under `/api/v1/` it did not route, and the editorial module answers everything under its own `/api/v1/editorial/` prefix the same way: a known path reached with the wrong method is 405 with an `Allow` header, anything else is 404, both in problem+json. The editorial prefix used to be the one corner where the router's `text/plain` answer broke the single error convention; that corner is closed, and the convention holds everywhere under `/api/v1/`.

**Completeness.** Every operation described here is served by the binary, and every route the binary registers is described here; a test in the composition root compares the two in both directions on every build.

**Availability.** The editorial routes are mounted only when the deployment configures JWKS verification; without it they answer 404 rather than authenticating nobody. The reader endpoints and the probes mount unconditionally.

servers.description: The internal service address inside compose and Kubernetes; the Astro server reaches it as API_BASE_URL.
A locally run binary (HTTP_ADDR defaults to :8080).

tags.name: reader
tags.description: Public, unauthenticated reads. Only published, non-withdrawn articles are visible.

tags.name: editorial
tags.description: Editorial writes. Bearer JWT plus the editor role on the account behind the token.

tags.name: operations
tags.description: Probes and tooling: liveness, readiness and this document.

tags.name: account
tags.description: A signed-in person's own state. Bearer JWT and nothing more: every route acts on the caller's own row, so there is no role that could be insufficient.

tags.name: cashback-ops
tags.description: Cashback operator queues and decisions. Bearer JWT plus the operator role on the account behind the token - the same authority the database requires of a payout approver (migration 0019).

tags.name: cashback-member
tags.description: A signed-in member's own cashback actions. Bearer JWT and nothing more: every route acts on the caller's own click, so there is no role that could be insufficient - only an account, which FR-023 requires.

get.summary: Where the caller got to in each guided tour
get.description:
Progress lives on the account rather than in the browser so a tour does not restart on a second device, and does not vanish when somebody clears site data.

The whole /api/v1/account/ prefix sits behind one auth gate, so a request without a usable token answers 401 whether or not the path exists.

200.description: The caller's progress, `{}` when no tour has been started.

401.description: No bearer token, or one that verifies for nobody provisioned here.

404.description: The token verifies but the account behind it no longer exists.

500.description: The progress could not be read.

put.summary: Record where the caller got to in one tour
put.description:
Idempotent: the cursor is a position, not an increment, so a repeated write of the same value changes nothing.

An account may track a bounded number of tours. Updating one it already tracks always succeeds; adding a new one past the limit answers 409 rather than growing the row without end.

parameters.name: tour
parameters.description: The tour's id, as defined in the front end.

cursor.description: A step index as a string, or "done" once the tour is finished or dismissed.

400.description: A tour id outside the permitted shape, a cursor that is neither "done" nor a step number, or a body that is not a single JSON document with just that field.

401.description: No bearer token, or one that verifies for nobody provisioned here.

404.description: The token verifies but the account behind it no longer exists.

409.description: This account already tracks the maximum number of tours, and this id is not one of them.

500.description: The progress could not be recorded.

get.description:
The article page payload: the feed item shape plus `approved_at`.

Unknown, unpublished, withdrawn and syntactically invalid ids are one indistinguishable 404 - the existence of unpublished work is not public, so a malformed id is not even answered with a 400.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The article id. A value that is not a UUID answers 404, not 400.

404.description: No article is visible under this id.

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: no such article

post.summary: Create a tracked click and get the redirect target
post.description:
Records the click and its rate snapshot, then answers where to send the member (FR-020, FR-021).

The click is committed before this response is written, and nothing is committed when the redirect cannot be built - so a 502 here means it is safe to try again. An anonymous click is never created: without a usable token the request is refused before anything is read (FR-023).

A member or device clicking far too often is refused with 429 and a Retry-After, and nothing is recorded then either (US7 scenario 1).

The whole path is unmounted when cashback is off, and then answers 404.

400.description: A body that is not this endpoint's shape, or an offer_id that is missing or not a UUID.

409.description: The offer is not published at this moment: expired, not yet started, or its retailer is no longer active.

429.description: Too many click-outs from this member, or from this device where the deployment can tell devices apart (US7 scenario 1). Nothing was minted and nothing was recorded, so waiting and trying again leaves the caller exactly where they were.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the rule lifts, rounded up: the moment the oldest click in the window falls out of it. Never zero.

502.description: No redirect could be built for this offer's network, so nothing was recorded and trying again later is safe.

get.summary: One retailer's page, with every rate band published for them
get.description:
The retailer at this address, described in the reader's language, with EVERY rate band in force right now - each carrying its own conditions and its own exclusions (US5 scenario 3, FR-011).

**Every rate here is what the MEMBER earns**, never the network's commission. A published band records the commission and, separately, the share of it the member receives; this endpoint composes the two before answering, rounding the way the credit itself will round, so the figure shown and the figure later paid can only differ over the commission the network actually reported.

**Bands are the published route's.** A retailer live on several networks has a band per network; the catalogue publishes one route, which is the route a click is issued through. Quoting the others would quote a rate no click can earn.

**An empty `rates` list is an ordinary answer.** A retailer whose bands have lapsed pays nothing today and is still a shop that exists, so it is 200 with no rates - never a 404.

**Language and place are independent axes** (constitution VII). `lang` names the language only. A merchant with no copy in it falls back to the retailer's source language and says so in `name_is_fallback` - an unrecognised or absent `lang` does the same rather than failing, because a page a member has navigated to should render.

The whole path is unmounted when cashback is off, and then answers 404.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The retailer's stable, human-readable address.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: BCP-47 primary language subtag the reader wants the copy in. Absent or unavailable falls back to the retailer's source language, labelled.

404.description: No retailer is published at this address: never imported, or imported and since paused. The two are one answer deliberately - which retailers we have stopped publishing is not a page request's business.

get.summary: List network transactions that matched no click
get.description:
The work an operator has to decide (FR-034, FR-060). A row is listed only while it is still work: nobody has resolved it, the report it names is still what the network last said about the transaction, and nothing has been credited against it.

The whole /api/v1/cashback/ops/ prefix sits behind one auth gate, so a request without a usable token answers 401 whether or not the path exists. The prefix is unmounted entirely when cashback is off, and then answers 404.

400.description: Unparseable limit (outside 1-100), a cursor this endpoint did not issue, or an unrecognised query parameter.

post.summary: Close an unattributed transaction without crediting anybody
post.description:
Records who closed the row and why, and publishes that fact, in one transaction (FR-061). Nothing is edited and nothing is deleted: a resolution can be written but never erased, so a mistaken one is corrected by a new fact in the stream rather than by a second call here - which is why replaying a dismissal answers 409 rather than repeating it.

Attributing a transaction to a member is not yet served: it writes a cashback.entry, which needs the member's share and a ledger posting the earnings module owns.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The queue row, as returned by the listing.

400.description: An id that is not a UUID, a body that is not this endpoint's shape, or a blank reason.

404.description: No queue row has this id. A queue row is never deleted, so this id was never issued.

409.description: The row is no longer open work: somebody has closed it, an entry now cites the report it names, or the network has replaced that report. The detail says which.

post.summary: Approve a withdrawal and submit the payout
post.description:
Release one withdrawal to the payout rail (US4 scenario 3, C-4, C-5).

There is no request body, and that is the contract rather than an omission: who approves is the token subject and when is the clock, so a body could only be naming an approver - which is exactly what C-4 forbids. One that arrives is refused with 400.

The approval is written and COMMITTED before the rail is contacted, because the payout's idempotency key is generated from the request and committing the row is what claims it. A second approval then loses on a unique violation rather than making a second payment.

So a rail failure answers 502 and the approval STANDS: the payout exists, its key is fixed, and a retry re-submits under it (FR-053). An operator told the approval had failed would approve it again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The withdrawal request being approved.

400.description: The id in the path is not a UUID, or a request body was sent.

404.description: No withdrawal request has that id.

409.description: The request is no longer awaiting approval, has already been paid, cannot be paid as one payout because its reserved entries span two brands (ADR-0004), or was refused by the schema - which includes an approver who does not hold the operator role (C-4).

502.description: The approval is recorded and the payout exists, but the rail did not accept it. It will be retried under the same key; do not approve again.

post.summary: Refuse a withdrawal and release its reservation
post.description:
Refuse one withdrawal and put its money back (US4 scenario 5, FR-061).

The reserved entries move back to confirmed under ONE ledger transfer, distinct from the reservation's own - so the member is exactly where they were before asking, and can ask again.

One transaction, unlike approving: an approval has to reach a payout rail and a rail is in no transaction, so it commits before it submits. A refusal touches nothing outside this database except the ledger.

Who refuses is the token subject and is not in the body. The reason is, and is required: withdrawal_request_rejection_has_reason refuses a rejected row without one, and a member is owed an explanation for money they did not get.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The withdrawal request being refused.

200.description: The refusal, and what went back.

400.description: The id in the path is not a UUID, the body is not a single JSON document of the expected shape, or the reason is blank or longer than 2000 characters.

404.description: No withdrawal request has that id.

409.description: The request is no longer awaiting approval, or its reservation moved no entries so there is nothing to release - the second needs looking at rather than deciding.

post.summary: Import a network's payment statement and derive its differences
post.description:
Records the statement verbatim and immutably as a reconciliation run (C-3), with who imported it, then lays it beside the current reports for the same publisher account and records every disagreement (US6 scenario 1): a confirmed report in the period no line paid, a line paying a report a different figure than it is owed, and a line naming no report at all.

The same statement for the same account and period imported again is the same run, answered 200 rather than 201, and detection runs again recording only what the first pass did not - so a retry of an upload that timed out is safe. The document is read in full before anything is written: a statement whose lines cannot be read is refused with 400 naming the line, because the row it would land in cannot be corrected afterwards.

Importing moves no money and changes no entry. The differences it records keep the affected transactions from confirming (FR-043) until an operator resolves them.

201.description: The statement became a new run; detection has run over it.

200.description: This exact statement for this account and period was already imported; this is that run, with detection run again.

400.description: A body that is not this endpoint's shape or is larger than 4 MiB, an account id that is not a UUID, a period end that is not a timestamp or is not after the start, a document without a `lines` array, or a line that names no transaction, names one twice, or states what it paid in anything but minor units and a currency. The detail names the line and the field.

404.description: No publisher account has this id.

413.description: The body is larger than 4 MiB.

get.summary: The differences a reconciliation run produced
get.description:
Every disagreement between the statement and the reports, oldest first, each with the figures behind it and the money as a delta - what was paid less what was owed, negative for a shorted or unpaid report, positive for an overpayment or money nothing expected. Resolved rows stay listed with their decision; `superseded` flags a difference filed against a report the network has since restated, so an operator knows the disagreement is with what the network used to say.

Paged like every operator queue: a `next_cursor` is present only when a further page exists.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The run, as returned by the import.

200.description: One page of the run's differences.

400.description: A run id that is not a UUID, a limit outside 1-100, an unknown or repeated query parameter, or a cursor this endpoint did not issue.

404.description: No reconciliation run has this id.

post.description:
Records who decided, what, why and when, together and once, and publishes that fact in the same transaction (FR-061). Either verdict lifts the difference from the confirmation gate (FR-043): `explained` - another fact accounts for the disagreement and nothing is owed either way; `absorbed` - the delta is the business's to bear or to keep, and the member's figure stands as reported.

There is deliberately no verdict for "the network owes us and we are chasing it": an open difference is the chase, and it keeps the gate shut until the money arrives or the network restates the report. Nothing else moves: any member-facing effect of a disagreement is a new posting resting on the network's own restated report (C-3), never on an operator's reading of it.

The acting account is the token subject and is never part of the body. A row is decided once; a second decision answers 409 naming the first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The difference, as listed.

200.description: The recorded decision, read back rather than echoed.

400.description: An id that is not a UUID, a body that is not this endpoint's shape, a verdict other than `explained` or `absorbed`, or a blank reason.

404.description: No difference has this id. Rows are never deleted, so this id was never issued.

409.description: Somebody already decided this difference. The detail says who, what and when.

get.summary: Export the caller's own cashback history
get.description:
The member's complete cashback history as one document, in JSON or CSV (FR-003).

FR-003 pairs leaving with taking your record, and for a reason: a member deciding whether to go should not have to choose between the two.

This is NOT a page. GET /wallet/entries pages because a member reads their history a screen at a time; an export is read by a spreadsheet, an accountant or a subject-access request, and a partial one is worse than none - a document that looks complete and is not. So there is no state, limit or cursor, and sending one is a 400 rather than a narrower file.

The CSV carries each money figure as TWO columns, minor units and currency, because C-6 holds in a spreadsheet exactly as on the wire: one column of bare integers is a column somebody sums across currencies. Text a spreadsheet would read as a formula is prefixed with an apostrophe - merchant names come from an affiliate network's catalogue and reasons are typed by operators, and neither is text this service wrote.

Both renderings are sent as an attachment, newest entry first.

The member is the bearer of the token. There is no path segment and no query parameter naming an account, so exporting somebody else's history is not a request this endpoint can express.

The whole path is unmounted when cashback is off, and then answers 404.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: json (the default) or csv.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: BCP-47 primary language subtag to name merchants in. A name shown in another language is labelled as a fallback rather than passed off (US5 scenario 2). Omitted, every name comes back labelled.

schema.description: A header row followed by one row per entry, newest first: entry_id, transacted_at, merchant_name, merchant_name_language, merchant_name_is_fallback, sale_amount_minor, sale_currency, cashback_amount_minor, cashback_currency, state, hold_rule, reversal_of_id, reason. An absent value is an empty cell.

400.description: An unknown query parameter, a format that is not json or csv, or a state, limit or cursor - which this endpoint refuses by name, because an export is always the complete history.

413.description: This history holds more entries than one document can carry. Refused rather than shortened: a CSV cut short is indistinguishable from a complete shorter one, so a member handed one would have a file they believe is their record and is not.

get.summary: Read the caller's own cashback participation
get.description:
Whether this member is in cashback, which version of the terms they accepted and when (FR-001, FR-002), and - if they have left - the date they left (FR-003).

What the ROW says, never today's configuration: a member who joined under an earlier revision of the terms is shown the revision they actually accepted.

The member is the bearer of the token. There is no path segment and no query parameter naming an account, so reading somebody else's participation is not a request this endpoint can express.

The whole path is unmounted when cashback is off, and then answers 404.

404.description: This account has never opted into cashback. Not an error condition: it is how a client knows to render the opt-in.

post.description:
Accept the terms in force and join cashback (FR-002). A member who left and comes back re-joins through this same endpoint, accepting whatever revision is in force then.

The version in the body must be the one this deployment is offering. A stale consent is never recorded: a member who agreed to last quarter's terms agreed to something they were not shown, and the 400 names the version that is in force so a client never has to guess.

The brand a member joins is frozen on the record. A deployment that is later rebranded does not move an existing participation between brands (ADR-0004).

400.description: The body is not a single JSON document of the expected shape, or terms_version is not the version in force. The detail names the version that is.

409.description: This account is already in cashback. Their acceptance stands as recorded; a second one would move the date and the version, which are the whole of the record.

503.description: This deployment has not configured a brand definition (BRAND_DIR), so there are no terms to offer and no brand to record an acceptance against. Nothing is broken; the deployment is incomplete.

delete.description:
Close this member's participation (FR-003).

Nothing financial is touched. Entries already earned continue to resolve, payouts already made stand, and the record is closed rather than deleted - the schema refuses the delete outright, because the evidence and the accounting outlive the preference.

200 rather than 204, because leaving has a date and the member is owed it. Idempotent: a second call answers the same participation with the same date.

404.description: This account has never opted into cashback, so there is nothing to leave.

get.summary: Read the caller's own cashback wallet
get.description:
Where the member's money is, what they have been paid, and what they must reach before asking to be paid again (FR-041, FR-050).

Every total is computed from ledger postings on each read, never from a stored balance (D7). paid_out is the exception and is not a balance at all: money that has been paid has left the business, so no account holds it and it is summed from the settled payouts instead.

The member is the bearer of the token. There is no path segment and no query parameter naming one, so reading another member's wallet is not a request this endpoint can express.

Money held back by a rule (US7) is deliberately not a total here. A hold is the business deciding not to count money yet, and a fifth figure would invite the member to count it; the entry itself carries the rule that is holding it.

The whole path is unmounted when cashback is off, and then answers 404.

503.description: This deployment has not configured a withdrawal threshold (PAYOUT_THRESHOLD_MINOR, PAYOUT_THRESHOLD_CURRENCY), so there is no currency to answer in and no figure to compare a balance against. Nothing is broken; the deployment is incomplete.

get.summary: List the caller's own cashback entries
get.description:
The purchases behind the totals: what was bought, what it earned, and what became of it (US3).

Reversals are listed as entries of their own alongside the credit they undo, with the reason the money went back. Neither half is hidden: a list showing only the reversal would look like a credit that never happened, and one showing only the original would leave a balance nobody could reconcile against it.

Newest first, paged by an opaque cursor rather than an offset. Entries are written while a member reads - a poll runs, a network confirms - and an offset would show them a row twice or skip one. Send back what next_cursor gave you; a cursor this endpoint did not issue is refused rather than silently answered with the first page.

The member is the bearer of the token, exactly as for GET /wallet.

The whole path is unmounted when cashback is off, and then answers 404.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: List only entries in this state. Omitted lists every state. A state no entry can be in is refused rather than answered with an empty page, because an empty page reads as "you have earned nothing".

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many entries to return. Defaults to 20; anything above 100 is capped rather than refused.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: the next_cursor of a previous page, echoed back unchanged. Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: BCP-47 primary language subtag to name merchants in, e.g. "el". A merchant with no copy in it is named in its own language instead, and the item says so - see merchant_name_is_fallback.

200.description: One page of the member's entries, newest first.

400.description: A query parameter this endpoint does not serve, a limit that is not a positive whole number, a state no entry can be in, or a cursor this endpoint did not issue.

post.description:
Reserve confirmed cashback and record a request for an operator to approve (US4, FR-050, FR-051).

The reservation happens in the SAME transaction as the request (D9), before any human reviews it, because the double-spend window is between request and approval. Two concurrent requests for the whole balance therefore produce one 201 and one 409: the second reads what the first left.

The member is the bearer of the token. There is no path segment and no query parameter naming an account, so asking to be paid out of somebody else's balance is not a request this endpoint can express.

The whole path is unmounted when cashback is off, and then answers 404.

201.description: The request, with what was reserved for it.

400.description: The body is not a single JSON document of the expected shape, the amount is not a positive {minor, currency}, or the currency is not one this deployment pays out in.

403.description: The destination is not the caller's. A destination that does not exist answers the same way, so an id cannot be probed for existence one request at a time.

409.description: The request cannot be met. `code` is `insufficient_confirmed_balance` - carrying `shortfall`, and `threshold`/`confirmed` or `confirmed`/`requested` - or `destination_not_verified` for a destination of the caller's own that has not been proved theirs (FR-051).

503.description: This deployment has not configured a withdrawal threshold or the house account earnings are paid out of. Nothing is broken; the deployment is incomplete, and the log names the keys.

get.description:
Every withdrawal this member has asked for, newest first, with the operator's decision where one has been made and the rail's reference where a payment has been submitted.

The member is the bearer of the token; reading somebody else's is not a request this endpoint can express.

One request of the caller's own.

A request belonging to somebody else and one that does not exist both answer 404, so an id cannot be probed for existence one request at a time.

400.description: The id in the path is not a UUID.

404.description: No withdrawal request of the caller's has that id.

get.description:
Every destination this member has recorded, oldest first, with whether each has been proved theirs (FR-051).

No bank details appear in the response and none ever will: they live outside this service (ADR-0003).

The member is the bearer of the token; there is no path segment or query parameter naming an account.

post.description:
Record a payout destination. It arrives UNVERIFIED, always: verification is a separate flow (FR-051), and one that arrived verified would be one nobody proved belongs to the member.

The details are handed straight to this deployment's details store and never held here; what is recorded is a reference (ADR-0003). They are not echoed in the response, not logged, and not quoted in a refusal.

The member is the bearer of the token; there is no field naming an account.

503 when the deployment has no details store configured. Only this endpoint needs one: listing destinations and withdrawing to those that already exist keep working.

400.description: The body is not a single JSON document of the expected shape, the kind is not one this deployment pays out on, the details are missing, or the details store refused them. The refusal never quotes what was sent.

502.description: The details store did not answer. Nothing was recorded, so the request can be repeated.

503.description: This deployment has no details store configured, so it has nowhere to put bank details. Nothing is broken; the deployment is incomplete, and the log says so.

post.summary: Approve an origin, optionally publishing it
post.description:
Approval creates the article; this endpoint carries the intent and the database enforces the rules.

**403 and 409 are the database's verdicts.** The insert trigger raises when the approver does not hold the editor role - the HTTP gate checked already, so a 403 here means the role changed under the request. The 409 comes from the one-per-origin unique indexes, with no application pre-check in front of them: a pre-check would disagree with the database exactly under the concurrency that makes the answer matter.

**Withdrawn origins may be approved again.** Those indexes are partial on `withdrawn_at IS NULL`, so an origin whose only articles are withdrawn is free - that is the documented correction flow, not a loophole.

**Side effects.** `article.approved`, and `article.published` when `publish` is true, are written to the append-only domain event stream in the same transaction as the article itself.

translated.summary: Approve a translation and publish it now

untranslated.summary: Approve a same-language item, releasing it later

400.description: Malformed JSON or an unknown field; both or neither origin supplied; an origin id that is not a UUID or names nothing; a blank attribution; or an untranslated origin whose feed provided no title, which would leave nothing to render as a headline.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: supply translation_id or source_item_id, not both: an article has exactly one origin

titlelessOrigin.summary: An untranslated item with no title

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: this item's feed provided no title, so an untranslated approval would have no headline; approve a translation of it instead

409.description: The origin already has a non-withdrawn article. Refused by the partial unique index, so two concurrent approvals of one origin produce exactly one 201 and one 409.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: this origin already has a published or approved article; withdraw it before approving a correction

get.summary: The five-minute audit of one article
get.description:
The full provenance chain (US5, FR-010), answered from the `article_provenance` view in a single query (I-5): source identity, the retrieval evidence with its licence snapshots, translation lineage with its recorded cost, the named approver, publication, and any withdrawal - audit sees full history, so withdrawn articles answer too.

**The legal basis is the snapshots.** `source_item` carries the licence terms, usage rule and permission evidence exactly as they applied at retrieval, written by trigger in the same transaction as the content (I-2, I-4). The `source` object is identity only; the mutable source row is never the legal basis of anything already retrieved.

**Events.** The article's rows of the append-only `domain_event` stream (FR-012), oldest first, each carrying the recorded payload as its detail. They arrive in the same statement as the chain - one round trip, one snapshot.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The article id. A value that is not a UUID answers 400 - a malformed id is a client mistake worth naming, distinct from an article that does not exist.

400.description: The `{id}` path segment is not a UUID.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: the article id in the path must be a uuid

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: no article with this id

post.description:
Publishes an article approved with `publish: false`. The database permits `published_at` to be set exactly once, and the statement guards on it, so two concurrent callers produce exactly one 200 and one 409.

**The actor must still be an editor at the moment of the write.** This is the one editorial write no trigger can guard - nothing on the article row records who released it - so the publishing transaction takes a locking read of the actor's account row and the UPDATE itself carries the editor predicate. A demotion and a publication therefore serialize rather than race, and a demoted account gets 403 with nothing published.

**Side effect.** `article.published` in the same transaction.

An article that was approved and never released stays that way permanently unless this endpoint is called: a frozen record of an approval, which withdrawal does not apply to.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The article id. A value that is not a UUID answers 400 here - a malformed id is a client mistake worth naming, distinct from an article that does not exist.

400.description: The `{id}` path segment is not a UUID.

malformedID.summary: A path id that is not a UUID

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: the article id in the path must be a uuid

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: no article with this id

409.description: The article is already published. Publication is one-way and happens once.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: this article is already published; publication happens once and is never repeated

post.summary: End a publication, preserving every record
post.description:
Withdrawal ends publication and destroys nothing (FR-016, I-5). The article row, its approval, its approver, its attribution and the retrieved evidence stay exactly as they were; there is deliberately no way to erase an approval.

**One guarded statement.** The update requires the article to be published and not yet withdrawn, so two concurrent withdrawals produce exactly one 200 and one 409 and neither meets the database's exception - the loser simply matches no row.

**The origin comes back.** The one-per-origin indexes are partial on `withdrawn_at IS NULL`, so a withdrawn article frees its origin and it reappears in the review queue flagged as a correction candidate, carrying this withdrawal in its history.

**Side effect.** `article.withdrawn`, carrying who and why, written by a database trigger in the same statement - so the audit record cannot be lost to application discipline, and the endpoint emits none of its own.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The article id. A value that is not a UUID answers 400 - a malformed id is a client mistake worth naming, distinct from an article that does not exist.

400.description: Malformed JSON or an unknown field, a blank reason, or an `{id}` path segment that is not a UUID.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: reason is required and must not be blank: a withdrawal is part of the audit record, and an unexplained one explains nothing

404.description: No article with this id, or one that was never published - withdrawal ends a publication, and an approval that was never released has none. Both answer 404: the existence of unpublished work is not something this endpoint confirms either.

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: no article with this id

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: no published article with this id

409.description: The article is already withdrawn. Withdrawal is one-way and final: who withdrew it, when and why is frozen once recorded.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: this article is already withdrawn; withdrawal is one-way and final, and who withdrew it, when and why is frozen

get.summary: List origins awaiting an editorial decision
get.description:
Retrieved items and their translations that have no non-withdrawn article. Origins whose only articles were withdrawn reappear here as correction candidates, carrying their withdrawal history.

The whole /api/v1/editorial/ prefix sits behind one auth gate, so a request without a usable token answers 401 whether or not the path exists.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Optional filter: only origins whose translation targets this language, plus untranslated origins in it.

400.description: Unparseable limit (outside 1-100), malformed lang, a cursor this endpoint did not issue, or an unrecognised query parameter.

403.description: The account is not an editor.

get.summary: List registered sources and their poll state
get.description:
The registered feeds, newest registration first, keyset-paginated on (created_at, id), with the last poll cycle summed from each active source's poll state - so the screen's cycle numbers are readings, not invented figures.

**The licensing fields are the CURRENT row, and the payload says so.** The legal basis of anything already retrieved is the retrieval-time snapshot on `source_item` (I-4), which the provenance endpoint serves and this list deliberately does not.

`permission_evidence` is returned, behind the editor gate: the screen exists to make the licensing basis visible, and it is what separates a lawful `full_text` source from an impossible one.

Unknown and repeated query parameters are rejected with 400, like the queue's.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Filter to polled (`true`) or paused (`false`) feeds - `source.active` is the operator's pause switch, and this list is its one read path. Exactly `true` or `false`; any other value is a 400. Absent means no filter.

200.description: One page of the source list, with the last poll cycle.

400.description: Unparseable limit (outside 1-100), an `active` that is not exactly true or false, a cursor this endpoint did not issue, or an unknown or repeated query parameter.

post.description:
Registers a feed the crawler may poll. The usage rule is not an input: every new source is `extract_and_link`, and upgrades are a separate founder-gated flow outside alpha scope. Sending `usage_rule` - any value, `null` included - is a 400 rather than a silently ignored field, as is any other unknown field.

The whole `/api/v1/editorial/` prefix sits behind one auth gate, so a request without a usable token answers 401 whether or not the path exists. Behind the gate the module's catch-all answers a wrong method with a problem+json 405 carrying `Allow`, and an unknown path with a problem+json 404, like everywhere else under `/api/v1/`.

value.name: Example Weekly
value.licence_terms: Extract and link permitted with attribution.

201.description: The source as the database recorded it.

400.description: Malformed JSON, an unknown field (`usage_rule` included), a blank required field, a `url` that is not an absolute http(s) URL with a host, or a language code the database does not know.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: usage_rule is not accepted: new sources are always extract_and_link; upgrades are a separate founder-gated flow

unfetchableURL.summary: A URL the crawler could never poll

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: url must be an absolute http or https URL with a host, e.g. https://example.org/feed.xml

409.description: A source with this feed URL is already registered.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: a source with this feed URL is already registered

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The source id, as `GET /api/v1/editorial/sources` listed it. A segment that is not a uuid is a 400 naming the mistake, not a 404 suggesting the source merely does not exist.

patch.description:
Applies any subset of `name`, `url`, `active` and `licence_terms`. Edits are licensing events: every PATCH that changes anything appends a `source.updated` domain event whose payload records the changed fields with their old and new values - for `licence_terms` and `url` especially, because "what did we believe the terms were, when" is exactly the question the audit stream exists to answer (I-4). The CURRENT row changes; the retrieval-time snapshots on `source_item` are untouched, so the legal basis of anything already retrieved never moves.

`active=false` is the everyday "remove": polling stops, default views hide the feed, and the history stays intact.

Each supplied field passes the same validation as registration - blank values and unpollable URLs are refused with the registration's own words. `usage_rule` is not editable here (upgrades stay a founder-gated flow), so supplying it is the unknown-field 400 like any other field the contract does not name.

value.licence_terms: Extract and link permitted with attribution, per the 2026 agreement.

200.description: The source as the database now records it, in the list's row shape.

400.description: Malformed JSON, an unknown field (`usage_rule` included), an empty patch, a blank supplied field, a `url` that is not an absolute http(s) URL with a host, or an `{id}` segment that is not a uuid.

409.description: The new feed URL is already registered to another source.

delete.summary: Delete a source that no evidence references
delete.description:
Deletion destroys evidence, so the database refuses it wherever evidence exists: `source_item.source_id` references the source with no ON DELETE clause, and a source with retrieved items answers 409 naming the evidence count - the FK's own verdict (23503) on the wire, never an application guess. The refusal points at deactivation, which is the everyday "remove"; converting a refused delete into a deactivation is a different decision that belongs to the editor, so the API never does it silently.

A source that never yielded an item deletes with 204 and disappears from the list.

204.description: The source is deleted. Only ever answered for a source no `source_item` row references.

400.description: The `{id}` path segment is not a uuid.

409.description: Retrieved items reference this source as evidence, so the database refused the delete. The detail names the count and points at deactivation.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: this source cannot be deleted: 12 retrieved item(s) reference it as evidence, and deleting the source would destroy their provenance chain; deactivate it instead (PATCH active=false) to stop polling while the history stays intact

get.summary: Front-page feed for one language and one or more places
get.description:
Published, non-withdrawn articles, newest first, keyset-paginated on (published_at, id). Both axes are required: a reader always reads one language, and follows at least one place (repeat `place` to follow several - a diaspora reader follows two).

An article whose origin was translated renders the translation's headline and extract; an untranslated (same-language) origin renders the feed-provided title with an extract derived from the retrieved body at read time. Either way `lang` on every returned item equals the requested language.

An empty result is an empty `items` array with a 200, never an error.

400.description: Unknown `lang`, missing or unknown `place`, a `limit` outside 1-100 or a non-integer one, or a malformed `cursor`.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: unknown lang "fr": the reader languages are el and de

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: at least one place is required (repeat place= to follow several)

get.description: Serves the committed `api/openapi.json` verbatim - the bytes are embedded into the binary at build time, so the served document and the validated file can never differ.

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document describing this API.

schema.description: An OpenAPI 3.1 document - this one, byte for byte.

get.description: Answers 200 as long as the process is serving. It touches no dependency, so it never reports the database's state - that is what /readyz is for.
Pings the database. A failing ping answers 503 so an orchestrator stops routing traffic here without killing the process.

503.description: The readiness check failed; the body is the same shape, not problem+json.

post.summary: Record that a payment made by hand has landed
post.description:
Record that a payout an operator carried out themselves reached the member (FR-053, FR-061).

This is the manual rail's whole settlement path and there is no automatic alternative to it. The scheduled sweep asks each rail what became of the payments it took; the manual rail always answers "submitted", because a rail that guessed otherwise would report money as delivered on the strength of a clock. A person went to a bank, so a person says so.

The rail reference is what the BANK called the transfer. It replaces the `manual:` placeholder the submission recorded - the one that means nobody has made the payment yet - and it is what a member quotes and an auditor follows, so a settlement without it would say money landed and leave nothing to trace it by.

Who records it is the token subject and is not in the body, as with every operator action here. The amount is not in the body either: the payout froze it at approval, and a settlement that could restate it would be one that could pay a different sum.

The payout becomes `settled` and the request becomes `paid`, in one transaction. The approval is not touched - `decided_by` and `decided_at` stay as the approving operator left them, because a settlement is an observation and not a second decision.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The withdrawal request whose payment landed.

200.description: The payment as it now stands.

400.description: The id in the path is not a UUID, the body is not a single JSON document of the expected shape, or the rail reference is blank or longer than 200 characters.

404.description: No withdrawal request has that id, or it has no payout because nobody approved it.

409.description: The payment is not waiting on a rail - already settled, already failed, or never sent - or it cannot be settled as it stands. Reload before recording it.

503.description: This deployment has nowhere to record a settlement. Nothing is broken and the approval queue keeps working; only this route is affected.

bearerAuth.description: A JWT from the auth provider, verified against the configured JWKS. The subject must map to an account. Endpoints under /api/v1/editorial/ additionally require that account to hold the editor role, and the database enforces that rule again on write; endpoints under /api/v1/account/ require only that somebody is signed in, because they act on the caller's own row.

Place.name: place
Place.description: Place slug to follow. Repeat the parameter to follow several places in one feed (`?place=thessaloniki&place=berlin`).

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Absent means the default; anything that is not an integer in 1-100 is rejected with 400 rather than clamped.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque page cursor: pass back the `next_cursor` of the previous page. Its encoding is an implementation detail and may change; clients must treat it as bytes. Values over 256 characters, or ones that do not decode, are rejected with 400.

Unauthenticated.description: No bearer token, or one that is invalid, expired or belongs to no account.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer realm="editorial"`, with `error="invalid_token"` appended when a token was supplied but rejected.

value.title: Unauthorized
value.detail: a bearer token is required

NotEditor.description: The token authenticated, but the account behind it does not hold the editor role.

value.title: Forbidden
value.detail: the editor role is required

InternalError.description: The request failed for a reason the caller cannot act on. Internals stay in the log: the body carries no database or stack detail, and `detail` may be absent entirely.

NotOperator.description: The token authenticated, but the account behind it does not hold the operator role.

value.title: Forbidden
value.detail: the operator role is required

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details, as every handler in this API writes them.

type.description: Always `about:blank`, which per RFC 9457 makes `title` the plain rendering of the status code. No problem-type URIs are minted for this API.

title.description: The HTTP status text, e.g. `Bad Request`.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of this occurrence. Omitted when the server has nothing safe to say (notably on 500).

Health.title: Health
Health.description: The probe body. Not problem+json, even on 503: the probes predate the API surface and answer their own shape.

version.description: The release version of the build that answered, stamped at build time from the release tag. Omitted entirely by a build the release pipeline did not cut - an unversioned build says so rather than reporting an empty version. The release probe asserts this against the tag it deployed: a 200 from the previous container is still a 200, and only this field tells them apart.

FeedItem.title: FeedItem
FeedItem.description: One published article as the reader surface renders it. Extract-and-link only: never the full body, always the outbound `source_url`.

id.description: The article id; the path parameter of the article endpoint.

headline.description: The translation's headline, or the feed-provided title for an untranslated origin.

extract.description: The translation's extract, or one derived from the retrieved body at read time for an untranslated origin. May be empty when the feed carried no usable body.

lang.description: Language of the rendered text: the translation's target locale, or the source's language for an untranslated origin. On the front page it always equals the requested `lang`.

places.description: Slugs of every place the article is tagged to, sorted; an untagged article carries an empty array rather than null.

attribution.description: The composed attribution block, rendered verbatim.

source_url.description: The original article at the publisher - the outbound link.

Article.title: Article
Article.description: The article page payload: a feed item plus the moment an editor approved it.

approved_at.description: RFC 3339 in UTC. Approval precedes publication and is never erased.

FrontPage.title: FrontPage
FrontPage.description: One page of the feed. Both fields are always present.

items.description: Newest first. Empty when nothing is published for the requested axes.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

SourcePatch.title: SourcePatch
SourcePatch.description: One edit to a registered source: any subset of the editable fields, at least one of them. Unknown fields - `usage_rule` included, which stays a founder-gated flow - are rejected with 400, so a misspelled key is named rather than silently ignored. Each supplied field passes the same validation as registration.

name.description: The publication's name, as attribution will render it. Must not be blank.

url.description: The feed URL the crawler polls - still the uniqueness key, so a URL registered to another source is a 409. Old and new land in the source.updated event.

active.description: The operator's pause switch: false stops polling and hides the feed from default views while every record stays intact - the everyday "remove".

licence_terms.description: The terms currently on record. Changing them appends a source.updated event carrying old and new; retrieval-time snapshots never move (I-4).

NewSource.title: NewSource
NewSource.description: A source registration. Unknown fields are rejected, so a misspelled key is a 400 rather than a silent omission.

name.description: The publication's name, as attribution will render it. Must not be blank.

url.description: The feed URL the crawler polls. Must be an absolute http or https URL carrying a host; it is also the uniqueness key for a source.

language.description: The language the source publishes in; must exist in the language reference table.

jurisdiction.description: The legal jurisdiction the source publishes under.

licence_terms.description: The terms under which this material may be reused, recorded verbatim for the audit trail.

usage_rule.description: Always `extract_and_link` for a newly registered source - the endpoint does not accept any other value.

ListedSource.title: ListedSource
ListedSource.description: One registered source as the list shows it. The licensing fields are the CURRENT source row - the legal basis of anything already retrieved is the snapshot on `source_item` (I-4), served by the provenance endpoint, never by this list.

url.description: The feed URL the crawler polls - the same column the registration wrote, under one name across both source endpoints.

licence_terms.description: The terms currently on record - not the terms that applied to any given retrieval.

permission_evidence.description: The recorded written permission behind a full_text rule, or null when none is on record. Served behind the editor gate, deliberately: the list exists to make the licensing basis visible.

active.description: Whether the crawler currently polls this feed - the operator's pause switch, observable here and nowhere else.

last_polled_at.description: When the poll loop last completed an attempt, success or failure alike; null for a feed never polled.

PollCycle.title: PollCycle
PollCycle.description: The last poll cycle, summed from each ACTIVE source's poll-state columns - real readings, never invented figures. Paused sources are excluded: their state describes a poll no longer running.

retrieved.description: How many new items the last poll of each active source stored, summed.

duplicates_skipped.description: How many items the content fingerprint recognised as already on record (FR-014), summed.

failures.description: The names of the active feeds whose last poll failed, sorted by name; [] (never null) when every last poll succeeded.

SourceList.title: SourceList
SourceList.description: One page of the source list, with the last poll cycle beside it. All three fields are always present.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor to fetch the next page. null on the last page - an absent cursor always means the list is exhausted.

Withdrawal.title: Withdrawal
Withdrawal.description: One ended publication in an origin's history. Withdrawal preserves every record (FR-016), so the entry stays queryable for good.

QueueItem.title: QueueItem
QueueItem.description:
One origin awaiting an editorial decision: a retrieved item, with its translation when one exists. translation_id and the translated fields are null together, for an untranslated origin.

The evidence block - original text, author, declared publication date, content fingerprint, translation lineage and cost - is carried BEFORE the decision, because the approval is permanent and `article_guard` freezes the attribution at the click (I-1, I-4).

headline_original.description: source_item.original_title - null when the feed provided none.

licence_snapshot.description: The licence terms in force when this item was retrieved (I-4), not the source row today.

source_url.description: The original article at the publisher - the link the editor opens to check the evidence.

original_author.description: The author as the feed named them; null when it named none - absent stays absent, never invented (FR-002).

original_published_at.description: The publication date the feed declared, null when it declared none. The attribution default MUST come from this field: the attribution is frozen at approval, and a client that substitutes retrieved_at freezes the retrieval date in as the publication date.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the retrieved body, computed by the database (I-3) - the evidence's own fingerprint.

extract_original.description: The retrieved original reduced to bounded prose by the shared D9 rule: markup dropped, at most 300 runes, cut at a sentence boundary. Evidence beside the translation - never the unbounded raw body.

target_lang.description: translation.target_locale; null for an untranslated origin.

model.description: The translation lineage's model (FR-005); null for an untranslated origin.

prompt_version.description: The lineage's prompt version (FR-005); null for an untranslated origin.

cost_microusd.description: The provider-reported cost recorded at insert (FR-006), in micro-USD; null for an untranslated origin.

correction_candidate.description: True exactly when withdrawals is non-empty: the origin is back in the queue because its only articles were withdrawn, so the editor is looking at a correction rather than a first approval.

withdrawals.description: Newest first; [] (never null) for a fresh origin.

ReviewQueue.title: ReviewQueue
ReviewQueue.description: One page of the review queue. Both fields are always present.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor to fetch the next page. null on the last page - an absent cursor always means the queue is exhausted.

NewApproval.title: NewApproval
NewApproval.description: An editorial decision to publish. Exactly one origin: `translation_id` for a translated article, `source_item_id` for an untranslated one, mirroring the database's `article_exactly_one_origin`. Supplying both, neither, or an explicit `null` for both is a 400. The approver is always the authenticated editor and is deliberately not a field here.

source_item_id.description: The retrieved item being approved untranslated. Its `original_title` becomes the headline, so an item whose feed provided no title is refused with 400.

attribution.description: The attribution block rendered with the article, pointing back to the original publisher. Stored trimmed; never blank.

publish.description: Publish in the same transaction as the approval. When false the article is an approved record awaiting release.

places.description: Place slugs the article publishes to - the front page is scoped by place, so an article tagged to no place can never appear on any of them, and the database refuses such an article at commit. An unknown or repeated slug is a 400 naming it, and so is a blank slug - empty or whitespace-only; minLength catches only the former, the server refuses both.

Approval.title: Approval
Approval.description: The article the approval created. A row in `article` IS the approval (I-1): there is no draft state, and no path creates one without a named editor.

approved_by.description: The authenticated editor who approved it.

published_at.description: When publication began, or null on the `publish: false` path.

NewWithdrawal.title: NewWithdrawal
NewWithdrawal.description: The decision to end a publication. Only the reason is supplied: who withdrew it comes from the bearer token, never from the body.

reason.description: Why publication is ending. Part of the audit record, so a blank one is refused - an unexplained withdrawal explains nothing. Stored trimmed.

WithdrawalRecord.title: WithdrawalRecord
WithdrawalRecord.description: The recorded withdrawal. The article row, its approval, its attribution and the retrieved evidence all survive it (FR-016, I-5).

withdrawn_by.description: The authenticated editor who ended the publication.

reason.description: The justification as the database froze it into `article.withdrawal_reason` - guarded all-or-none with the other withdrawal columns and permanent once written. The record, not an echo of the request; never blank.

ArticleProvenance.title: ArticleProvenance
ArticleProvenance.description: The full audit chain of one article, from the `article_provenance` view in one query (I-5). The `source` object is identity only: the legal basis always comes from the retrieval-time snapshots inside `source_item` (I-4).

headline.description: The translation's headline, or the item's original title for an article published untranslated - the same resolution the reader sees.

places.description: Where the article published to, as sorted place slugs. Always a list, never null.

translation.description: The translation lineage, or null for an article published untranslated.

published_at.description: When publication began, or null for an approved-but-never-released record.

withdrawal.description: How publication ended, or null while it has not.

events.description: The article's rows of the append-only audit stream (FR-012), oldest first. Always a list, never null.

ProvenanceSource.title: ProvenanceSource
ProvenanceSource.description: The licensed feed's identity - and identity ONLY. No licence field belongs here: the source row is mutable, and the legal basis of what was retrieved is the immutable snapshots on `source_item` (I-4).

ProvenanceSourceItem.title: ProvenanceSourceItem
ProvenanceSourceItem.description: The immutable retrieval record (I-2, I-3): what was fetched, when, its database-computed fingerprint, and the licence terms exactly as they applied at retrieval, written by trigger in the same transaction as the content (I-4).

source_url.description: The original article at the publisher.

original_title.description: The item title exactly as the feed provided it, or null when it omitted one.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the retrieved body, computed by the database.

licence_snapshot.description: The licence terms as they applied at retrieval (I-4).

usage_rule_snapshot.description: The usage rule in force at retrieval.

permission_evidence_snapshot.description: The permission evidence on record at retrieval, or null when there was none.

original_author.description: The author as the feed named them, or null when it did not.

ProvenanceTranslation.title: ProvenanceTranslation
ProvenanceTranslation.description: The machine-translation lineage (FR-005): which model, which prompt version, when, and the provider-reported cost recorded at insert (FR-006).

ProvenanceApproval.title: ProvenanceApproval
ProvenanceApproval.description: The named human whose decision the article is (I-1).

ProvenanceWithdrawal.title: ProvenanceWithdrawal
ProvenanceWithdrawal.description: The recorded end of publication (FR-016): who, when and why, frozen once written.

ProvenanceEvent.title: ProvenanceEvent
ProvenanceEvent.description: One row of the append-only audit stream (FR-012). The detail is the recorded payload itself, compact, minus the article_id the response is already scoped to - the record, never a paraphrase.

TourProgress.description: Where this account got to in each guided tour. Always present and `{}` when none has been started, so a client never has to tell an absent field from an empty one.

tours.description: Tour id to cursor. The cursor is a step index as a string, or "done". The tours themselves are defined in the front end, so this API stores the value and does not interpret it beyond its shape.

Money.description: An amount of money: whole minor units and the ISO-4217 code they are denominated in. Never a decimal and never a float - the frontend formats these two fields for a locale, and nothing between here and there has to agree on how many decimal places a currency has (C-6).

minor.description: The amount in minor units, e.g. 4999 for 49.99 EUR.

UnattributedTransaction.description: One network report that matched no click, waiting for an operator (FR-034). Every field is a fact the network reported or the database stamped; there is no recommended action, because what may lawfully be done with the row is `attributable`.

id.description: The queue row, and what an operator action names.

detected_at.description: When the poll that stored the report noticed it had no click reference.

network_transaction_id.description: The evidence row: the report an entry for this purchase would have to cite.

network_account_id.description: The publisher account whose poll found it.

external_id.description: The network's own transaction id, for finding it in their dashboard.

status.description: What the network last said about the transaction.

commission.description: What the network says it will pay; the member's share is computed from this (FR-040).

retrieved_at.description: When this report was read from the network.

attributable.description: Whether an entry could lawfully be created for this report at all. False where the network named a click reference that matched no click: a credit must cite the click the network named, and there is none - so dismissing is the only outcome the database will accept.

UnattributedQueue.description: One page of unattributed work, oldest first.

next_cursor.description: Null on the last page. Present only when a further page exists, so a cursor never leads to an empty one.

Dismissal.description: Why an operator is closing a queue row without crediting anybody. The acting account is taken from the bearer token and is never part of the body.

reason.description: The recorded reason (FR-061). Trimmed; a blank or whitespace-only reason is rejected with 400, because the audit record is part of the action.

Resolution.description: The resolution the database recorded, read back rather than echoed.

resolved_by.description: The operator account that closed it, taken from the token subject.

resolved_at.description: Stamped by the database, not supplied by the caller.

StatementPeriod.description: The half-open interval [start, end) a statement covers. Reports are matched to it on when the purchase happened, not on when it was polled.

end.description: Must be after start, once both are truncated to the microseconds the database keeps.

StatementImport.description: A network's payment statement as an operator imports it. The acting account is taken from the bearer token.

network_account_id.description: The publisher account the statement is for.

statement.description: The network's document, stored verbatim. `lines` is required - a statement that paid nothing says so with an empty list - and every line names one transaction once and says what was paid for it in minor units and a currency (C-6); a negative amount is a deduction. Any other member, here or on a line, is kept and ignored.

transaction_id.description: The network's own id for the transaction, as its reports carry it. Surrounding whitespace is removed.

DifferenceDetection.description: What the detection pass over the run derived and recorded.

found.description: Every difference derived this pass, recorded or already there.

recorded.description: How many of those were new rows. The rest were already recorded, resolved or not, and were not raised again.

ReconciliationRun.description: An imported statement, as recorded, and what detection made of it.

lines.description: How many payments the statement names.

statement_digest.description: md5 of the statement as stored, computed by the database. With the account and the period it is what makes a retried import the same run.

imported_by.description: The operator account, taken from the token subject.

already_imported.description: True when this exact statement for this account and period was here before this call; run_id, imported_by and imported_at are then the earlier import's.

DifferenceResolutionRecord.description: A recorded decision on a difference.

resolved_by.description: The operator account, taken from the token subject.

Difference.description: One disagreement between a statement and the reports.

network_transaction_id.description: The report named; null for money matching no report.

transaction_id.description: The network's own id for the transaction: the report's where one is named, the statement line's otherwise.

superseded.description: The network has restated the report this difference names since it was filed: the disagreement is with what the network used to say.

resolution.description: Null while the row is open.

DifferenceQueue.description: One page of a run's differences, oldest first.

next_cursor.description: Null on the last page. Present only when a further page exists, so a cursor never leads to an empty one.

DifferenceResolutionRequest.description: What an operator decided about a difference and why. The acting account is taken from the bearer token and is never part of the body.

resolution.description: explained: another fact accounts for the disagreement and nothing is owed either way. absorbed: the delta is the business's to bear or to keep.

reason.description: The recorded reason (FR-061). Trimmed; a blank or whitespace-only reason is rejected with 400.

DifferenceResolution.description: The decision the database recorded, read back rather than echoed.

resolved_by.description: The operator account that decided it, taken from the token subject.

resolved_at.description: Stamped by the database, not supplied by the caller.

NewClickOut.description: Which published band the member is clicking through. The member comes from the token and the rate from the offer: a body that could name either would be a body that could claim somebody else's click or a rate nobody published.

offer_id.description: The rate band to click through.

ClickOut.description: The tracked redirect. The click row and its rate snapshot are committed before this is written (FR-020), so the purchase that follows can always be matched back.

click_ref.description: The unguessable reference the network will echo back against the purchase, and the value every reported transaction is matched on (FR-020, FR-021). Returned so a support conversation can quote the same value the evidence carries.

redirect_url.description: Where to send the member. Absolute, http or https.

expires_at.description:
When the rate band this click was issued against stops being published, or null for a band with no published end.

About the OFFER, not the redirect: the credit this click earns is governed by the snapshot taken when it was issued, whatever happens to the band afterwards (FR-013), and no network expires a deeplink. It is the same window whose end makes a later click-out answer 409.

Merchant.description: A retailer's page: who they are, how they are described in the reader's language, and every rate band published for them at the moment the page was read.

slug.description: The address this page was reached at.

country.description: Where the retailer trades, or null when they are bound to no one country. Not where the reader is: language and place are independent axes (constitution VII).

name_language.description: The language the copy on this page is actually in, which is not necessarily the one that was asked for.

name_is_fallback.description: Whether the copy came from the retailer's source language because none exists in the reader's. This is how US5 scenario 2 renders "shown in German" rather than silently pretending.

typical_confirmation_days.description: How long a purchase here usually takes to confirm. ALWAYS null today: nothing in the schema records it - not on the retailer, not on the route, not on the network - and a member reads this number as "you will be paid in about six weeks", so it is left absent rather than filled in with a plausible constant.

rates.description: Every band in force right now, newest first. Empty when the retailer's rates have lapsed, which is an ordinary answer rather than a 404.

MerchantRate.description: One published rate band, as the member earns it. Exactly one of `bps` and `amount` is present, chosen by `kind`; both are integers, because no rate or money value on this API is ever a decimal string or a float (C-6). The frontend formats for display from these fields.

offer_id.description: The band a click on this rate would be issued against - the value POST /clickouts takes, so a page and the click it leads to name the same rate.

kind.description: Which of `bps` and `amount` carries this rate.

bps.description: The member's rate in basis points on a percent band (4% = 400). Absent on a fixed band.

amount.description: What the member earns per transaction on a fixed band. Absent on a percent band.

conditions.description: What this band requires, verbatim as published (FR-011), or null when it records none. Null rather than an empty string, so "no conditions" and "conditions that failed to load" do not render the same.

exclusions.description: What this band does not pay on (FR-011), or null when it records none.

valid_to.description: When this band stops being published, or null for one with no published end.

Wallet.description: A member's money, by stage, plus what they have been paid and the threshold a withdrawal is checked against. Every figure names its currency; they are always the same one, because a wallet is answered in the currency the deployment states its threshold in (C-6).

pending.description: Reported by a network and not yet confirmed. Visible, never spendable.

confirmed.description: Confirmed by the network AND accounted for by an imported statement (FR-043). The only figure the threshold applies to.

reserved.description: Claimed by a withdrawal request and no longer available to a second one (D9). Still the member's.

paid_out.description: The lifetime total of payments that settled. Not a balance: this money has left the business, and this is the record that it went. Payments in flight and payments that failed are not counted.

payout_threshold.description: What confirmed must reach before a withdrawal may be requested (FR-050). Returned rather than left to the client, so a client cannot show one figure while the server enforces another.

WalletEntry.description: One line of a member's history: the purchase, what it earned, and where that stands.

merchant_name.description: The retailer, or null for an entry an operator attributed by hand: there was no click, so there is no route to a retailer to follow (FR-034).

merchant_name_language.description: The BCP-47 primary subtag merchant_name is written in, or null when there is no name.

merchant_name_is_fallback.description: True when merchant_name is in the retailer's own language rather than the one asked for. US5 scenario 2 requires that to be shown as a fallback rather than passed off as the member's language.

transacted_at.description: When the purchase happened, as the network reported it - the instant a member recognises. Not when the entry was written.

expected_confirmation_at.description: When this entry is expected to confirm. ALWAYS null today: nothing in the schema records a confirmation window, so there is no honest value to compute, and an invented one is a date a member would plan around. It becomes a real answer when a window is recorded per route.

hold_rule.description: The rule holding this entry back, and null unless the state is held (US7). The wallet totals do not show held money at all, so a member looking at an entry they cannot count is owed the reason.

reversal_of_id.description: The entry this one undoes, and null on an entry that undoes nothing (SC-010).

reason.description: Why this entry exists, recorded with the transition that opened it. On a reversal, why the money went back.

WalletEntryPage.description: One page of a member's entries, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Where to continue from, or null when this page is the last. Null rather than a cursor that would return nothing, so a client stops by reading the answer rather than by making one more request to discover it.

Participation.description: A member's opt-in to cashback (FR-001). The record of which version of the terms they accepted and when (FR-002), plus - once they have left - the date they left. Leaving closes the record; it never deletes the financial rows built on it (FR-003).

status.description: Whether the member is currently in cashback. There is no third state and no pending: accepting the terms IS the opt-in.

opted_in_at.description: When they accepted. Re-stated when a member who left comes back, because coming back means accepting the terms in force then.

terms_version.description: Which revision of the terms this member accepted (FR-002). What the ROW says, which on an older participation may not be the version in force today.

default_currency.description: The currency this member's wallet is denominated in, as an explicit ISO-4217 code (C-6). Taken from the brand's default at the moment of acceptance (ADR-0004).

left_at.description: When they left, or null while they are still in. Leaving is a status and a date, never a deletion.

ParticipationOptIn.description: An acceptance of the terms in force.

terms_version.description: The revision being accepted. It must be the one in force; a stale consent is never recorded, and the 400 names the version that is.

CashbackExport.description: A member's complete cashback history as one document (FR-003). Not a page: an export is the whole record or it is not an export, so this endpoint takes no state, limit or cursor.

exported_at.description: When this document was taken. The export walks the history backwards, so an entry written while it was being assembled is newer than the pages already read and is not in the file; this is what lets a reader tell what the document covers.

entry_count.description: How many entries follow. Written out rather than left to be counted, so a truncated file can be DETECTED: the count and the array would disagree.

entries.description: The whole history, newest first - the same order and the same item shape as GET /wallet/entries, so a client parses one thing for both.

CashbackWithdrawalRequest.description: A member asking to be paid their cashback. The member is the bearer of the token and is deliberately absent from the body: there is no field naming an account, so asking to be paid out of somebody else's balance is not a request this endpoint can express.

destination_id.description: One of the caller's own verified payout destinations (FR-051). A destination belonging to somebody else answers 403, and so does one that does not exist.

amount.description: What the member is asking for. What is actually reserved may be more - see reserved_amount.

CashbackWithdrawal.description: A cashback withdrawal request as it was recorded, with the reservation already made (D9).

state.description: Always awaiting_approval on creation: the money is reserved before any human reviews the request, and the review is an operator's act (C-4).

reserved_amount.description: What was actually moved out of confirmed, which is at least the amount asked for.
