Cashback is reserved in whole entries - each cites the network report evidencing it (C-2), so there is no half of one to take - and a member who asks for slightly less than an entry has slightly more reserved. This, not the amount requested, is what a payout will pay.

InsufficientConfirmedBalance.description: A problem document carrying the arithmetic as RFC 9457 extension members - `code`, `shortfall`, and the two figures it was derived from - so a client shows the member what would work instead of parsing prose. No figure appears in `detail`: amounts travel as {minor, currency} and the client formats them for the member's locale.

ApprovedPayout.description: One outbound money movement, as it stands the moment it was approved. The row IS the approval (C-4): it cannot exist without a named operator behind it.

approved_by.description: The operator this payment rests on, taken from the token subject and never from the request (C-4). Echoed so an operator sees which account the server recorded rather than which one they believe they are.

idempotency_key.description: The database's own derivation from the request (C-5, D8), never a value a caller supplied. It is what a retry must reuse and what an operator searches by on the rail's side.

rail.description: Which rail carried the money. Frozen once the row exists (payout_guard).

rail_reference.description: What the rail called this payment, and null until the rail has answered. A submitted payout without one is not broken: it is the state a retry picks up (FR-053).

WithdrawalRefusal.description: An operator refusing a withdrawal. Who refuses is the token subject and is deliberately absent from the body; the reason is not, because a member is owed an explanation for money they asked for and did not get.

reason.description: Why the withdrawal was refused (FR-061, US7 scenario 3). Required and non-blank - withdrawal_request_rejection_has_reason refuses a rejected row without one. Trimmed of surrounding whitespace and otherwise stored as given.

RefusedWithdrawal.description: A refused withdrawal: the decision, and the ledger movement that put the money back. Two facts, because an operator checking the second against the ledger needs its reference.

decided_by.description: The operator this refusal rests on, taken from the token subject. Echoed so they see which account the server recorded.

released_amount.description: What went back to confirmed balance - the sum of the entries the reservation held, which is the request's own amount (US4 scenario 5).

release_transfer.description: The ledger transfer that carried the money back. Distinct from the reservation that carried it out: one movement each way, each with its own reference. Sharing one would make the release a replay that recorded nothing.

WithdrawalSettlement.description: An operator saying a payment they made by hand has landed.

rail_reference.description: What the bank called the transfer, replacing the `manual:` placeholder recorded at submission.

SettledPayout.description: One payout that reached the member.

rail_reference.description: What the operator recorded, which is what a member quotes to their bank.

settled_at.description: Never null: payout_settled_iff_settlement_time ties the instant to the state.

request_state.description: Echoed so an operator reading one screen need not reload another to learn the member's request is paid.

PayoutDestination.description: Somewhere a member may be paid. It carries NO bank details and never will: the details live outside this service (ADR-0003) and an endpoint that echoed them would be the leak that arrangement exists to prevent.

kind.description: Which rail would carry the money.

verified_at.description: When the member proved this destination is theirs (FR-051), or null. A withdrawal to one that is null is refused with 409, so a client can tell before asking.

verified_method.description: How they proved it. Present exactly when verified_at is: "verified, method unknown" is not a verification anyone could defend later.

NewPayoutDestination.description: Somewhere to be paid, as a member sends it. The details go to this deployment's details store and what is recorded is the reference it answers with (ADR-0003); they are never stored here and never come back out of this API.

kind.description: Which rail should carry the money. It decides what counts as valid details.

details.description: What the rail needs to pay this member - an IBAN and a holder for sepa, a note for manual. Deliberately unconstrained here: what belongs in it differs by rail and the details store is the only thing positioned to judge, so this API does not restate a shape it does not enforce.

MemberWithdrawal.description: One withdrawal request as the member who made it reads it back.

amount.description: What was reserved, which is what a payout pays.

decided_at.description: When an operator decided it, or null while it waits.

decision_reason.description: Why it was refused. A member is owed an explanation for money they asked for and did not get (FR-061), so it reaches them here and not only the operator.

payout_reference.description: What the rail called the payment, null until a payout exists and the rail has answered. It is the string a member quotes to their bank.
